name: Oshiage
tagline: Tokyo in 17 minutes and Otemachi in 17 minutes. Served by 4 lines.
summary: The station is in Sumida City, served by Tobu Skytree Line, Keisei Oshiage Line, Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line and Toei Asakusa Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 17 minutes to Otemachi, 33 minutes to Shinjuku, 36 minutes to Shibuya and 31 minutes to Shinagawa. The station stands 2 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 2.6 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 2 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from -0.6 m to 2 m, a difference of 2.6 m. These figures were read from the elevation API of the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan at nine points: the station itself and eight compass directions 400 m out.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 9 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 9 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.

groceries.name: Poisson Okuda ポワソンオクダ

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 10 clinics and 12 pharmacies. Facilities recorded as hospitals lie at 健生堂病院, about 221 m away and 高石胃腸病院, about 829 m away. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 4 lines serve the station: Tobu Skytree Line, Keisei Oshiage Line, Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line and Toei Asakusa Line. The lines are split between operators (Tobu runs 1 line, Keisei runs 1 line, Tokyo Metro runs 1 line and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company. Scored out of 100 from the number of lines and the spread of operators, transfer convenience here comes to 90.

neighbours.lead: Oshiage is ahead on the number of lines.
neighbours.note: 326 m away in a straight line. It takes 6 minutes longer to reach Otemachi than Oshiage.

neighbours.lead: Honjo-Azumabashi is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Oshiage is ahead on the number of lines and the number of medical facilities.
neighbours.note: 786 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Oshiage.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 7 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Among the 23 wards' stations, comparatively many of the points around this one fall inside the projected inundation area for the largest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the ガーデン通り (a main road) runs 145 m away. Morning and evening, the cars are audible indoors serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
